intro: Rishabh's tutorials, courses and essays, put in an order a beginner can follow: Python first, then data, then a first model, then practice, then the business view.

steps.title: Python, for business students
steps.why: Both are written for business and analytics students.

items.title: Coding-For-MBA
items.note: A self-paced Python and data curriculum: 12 phases, 6 projects and 15 case studies, with code that runs in the browser.

items.title: Python Course, GIM BDA
items.note: Python course materials in Jupyter notebooks for Big Data Analytics students at GIM.

steps.title: A first data analysis
steps.why: One small dataset, start to finish: load it, look at it, ask it questions, chart the answer.

items.title: A Beginner's Guide to Data Analysis with Python: Using Pandas and NumPy
items.note: Works through the Iris dataset with read_csv, describe, boolean filters and groupby, then plots a bar chart with matplotlib.

steps.title: A first model
steps.why: It builds only on Pandas from the step before, and it names its own limit, the cold-start problem.

items.title: Build Your First Movie Recommendation Engine in Python
items.note: User-based collaborative filtering on MovieLens 100k: a user-item matrix, Pearson correlation to find similar users, and a weighted average of their ratings.

steps.title: Practice
steps.why: Two ways to practise: one small game built from start to finish, then a long list of challenges to pick from.

items.title: Python Game Development: Create a Basic 2D Game with Pygame
items.note: Builds Dodge the Blocks! step by step: a player, falling enemies, collision detection, a score and a game-over screen.

items.title: Programming-Challenges-6
items.note: 150 programming challenges across practical software, algorithms, web development, data analytics and applied machine learning.

steps.title: The business view
steps.why: Two essays that step back from code to the ideas behind AI and behind buying decisions.

items.title: 5 Surprising Ideas That Redefined Artificial Intelligence
6 Counter-Intuitive Marketing Truths That Explain Why We Buy
